newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court sentences 41 students, Amnesty protests.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court sentences 41 students, Amnesty protests.

text.p: A South Korean court sentenced 41 students on Friday for their part in violent pro-North Korean campus unrest in August, and Amnesty International condemned the Seoul government over the crackdown.

Fifteen of the students were jailed for between eight months and 2-1/2 years, six of them under national security laws that ban all unauthorised contact with communist North Korea. The court gave suspended sentences to another 26.
It was the second mass sentencing this week connected with the unrest at Seoul's prestigious Yonsei University during which a young riot policeman died. On Tuesday 110 students were convicted.
A total of 444 students, many of them members of a leftist student council, the Hanchongryon, have been charged.
Amnesty on Friday accused South Korean police of sexually assaulting arrested female students as part of widespread human rights abuses after riot police stormed Yonsei to end a seven-day occupation.
Subsequent efforts to stamp out left-wing ideology had led to an alarming rise in the number of political prisoners, the London-based human rights group said in a report.
"Police in South Korea were responsible for widepread and systematic ill-treatment after the students were arrested," the report said.
"Female students said that police had grabbed their breasts and other parts of their bodies and shouted sexual insults."

"At Seoul police stations students were forced to sit or kneel in the same position for hours. Some were beaten during police interrogation where they were forced to write a confession," the report said.

Government statements have since led to a "climate of intolerance against people with left-wing views", it said. "It is alarming that the number of political prisoners has escalated in recent months as the authorities try to stamp out left-wing thought."
Amnesty said the government must share some of the blame for the Yonsei violence and called for an independent inquiry into allegations of ill-treatment.
On Thursday, a member of the opposition Democratic Party, Lee Mi-kyung, demanded during a parliamentary session punishment for police involved in sexual misconduct.

"It's not that I agree with students who participated in the pro-North Korean rally," she said. "But I ask the government to provide an answer to accusations that the police sexually harassed the activist students."

Almost 6,000 students were detained after the worst campus unrest since President Kim Young-sam took power in 1993. Kim has branded the Hanchongryon a "terrorist" organisation and its leader was arrested on Monday.

Riot police stormed Yonsei to end an occupation of two teaching blocks by students taking part in an annual pro-Korean unification rally. They were also protesting against the presence of 37,000 U.S. troops in South Korea.
North and South Korea have been in armed confrontation since a 1953 truce ended the Korean War and sealed the World War Two division of the Korean peninsula.
